title: Horizon Gold targets resource growth at Gum Creek
summary: Horizon Gold Ltd managing director Scott Williamson talked with Proactive about broad, high-grade gold intersections returned from drilling at the Kingfisher, Hawk and Swan prospects within the Gum Creek Gold Project in Western Australia. The strongest result came from Kingfisher, where reverse circulation drilling intersected 23 metres at 5.26 g/t gold from 188 metres, including 15 metres at 7.65 g/t gold. Williamson said the result demonstrated the high-grade nature of the Kingfisher deposit and extended the mineralised area to the north, towards the Swan and Swift deposits. The intersection sits within the proposed open-pit mining area, meaning it could contribute to an expansion of the planned Kingfisher open pit. Horizon Gold is also continuing to test deeper mineralisation that may support future underground mining. He also discussed the potential economic impact of further resource growth. Horizon Gold’s recent study outlined a ten-year open-pit mining operation producing around 100,000 ounces of gold annually. Additional open-pit resources could extend that mine life, while the inclusion of underground mining could lift production above the 100,000-ounce-per-year level. Further drilling is planned to test underground potential at Swan and Kingfisher, while also continuing to extend the open pits. title: Dow, S&P 500 close at records on AI results, Mideast deal hopes
summary:
STORY: Wall Street's main indexes surged on Tuesday, with the Dow and S&P 500 both gaining roughly one-and-three quarters percent to notch record-high closes, and the Nasdaq climbing more than two-and-a-half percent.

Investors eagerly awaited SpaceX's first earnings results since its IPO, delivered after the close. Elon Musk's rocket and AI company reported a more than 90% rise in revenue for the quarter, buoyed by strong growth in its Starlink satellite-internet and AI businesses. The company posted a net loss of more than $540 million and capital expenditures of over $18 billion. Its shares, which closed up, gave back most of those gains in extended trading.

The stock, which has fallen 8% since SpaceX's record-breaking IPO in June, could face further pressure this week when the lock-up period expires, notes Rob Haworth, senior investment strategy director at U.S. Bank Asset Management Group.

"I think the market's probably a little worried that we're going to see more shares being offered, although we've been below the IPO price, so we'll have to see. But we think this remains a really important year for IPO markets as we have OpenAI and Anthropic coming as well. This will really start to unlock this private equity market and get some fresh capital to work. And then I think it's a question of how do markets adapt to this, right? How do markets adapt to all these new providers, which are model companies, and incorporate those into the overall ethos? So this is going to remain a really interesting year when it comes to some fresh blood into the U.S. equity market."

:: AMD

Also after the close, AMD said its second-quarter revenue rose 50% year-over-year, beating analysts' expectations. But the stock, which closed 7% higher, erased those gains in extended trading.

In other earnings news, Palantir Technologies grabbed headlines after its CEO delivered what he called "otherworldly" results, with the software company raising its annual revenue forecast. Shares skyrocketed more than 29% to record their biggest daily percentage gain since February of 2024.

:: Caterpillar

And shares of Caterpillar, seen as a bellwether for the global industrial economy, jumped about five-and-a-half percent after the company raised its annual revenue growth forecast, as the buildout of AI data centers has fueled demand for its power-generation and construction equipment.

Meanwhile, crude prices settled down about 5% after a Qatari official said efforts to secure a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict were continuing, while U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could come within the next two days.
